subject: Conditional residency exceptions and DPA gap logistics
messages:
From: Judy Smith <j.smith@greenbank.com>
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
Cc: compliance@greenbank.com
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Residency exceptions and DPA — initial questions

Hi Sergio,

Thanks for the call earlier. GreenBank is evaluating Redwood for a tiered KYC enrichment flow (token classification + embeddings) and we have a couple of potentially blocking privacy items before procurement can proceed:

- A handful of our regulated lines want a conditional exception to standard residency — they are comfortable with tokenized inputs leaving the US for ephemeral inference if (a) the model runs in a vetted EU/US region and (b) subprocessors are contractually restricted.
- We need to confirm whether Redwood can (i) provide a signed DPA with explicit GLBA clauses, (ii) accept residency exceptions on a per-entity basis in the same contract, and (iii) produce a subsystem-level dataflow map to show where unencrypted metadata is routed.

Can you send over your latest DPA redlines (we're on v3 internally) and a short dataflow mapping? Also helpful: a one-pager on how Redwood handles cross-border KV cache behavior and whether that could trigger residency violations.

I copied our compliance team (compliance@greenbank.com) and the DPO. If you prefer, we can route redlines via DocuSign and set up a 30-minute rubric call.

Appreciate quick confirmation — procurement has a narrow window.

Best,
Judy
Judy Smith
Sr. Procurement Manager — Cloud Risk
GreenBank Financial

Hi Judy — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Mina (privacy) and Karthik (product ops) to make sure we answer each item precisely. Quick summary / proposed next steps: 

1) DPA + GLBA: We can sign a DPA that includes GLBA-specific addenda language. I am attaching our current redline (GreenBank-DPA-redlines-v3.pdf) that calls out a GLBA addendum as a defined schedule. If you have specific clause language your counsel requires, please send and Mina will review.

2) Per-entity residency exceptions: We support per-account residency constraints via our Dedicated/Private offerings. For Hosted customers, we can accept limited conditional exceptions that are operationally scoped — i.e., we can restrict model execution to region X and enforce subprocessor constraints, but we cannot promise complete physical isolation unless the account is on Dedicated or Private. We can include a residency exception clause that lists precise operational limits (max datasets, allowed regions, KV cache TTL).

3) Dataflow mapping + KV cache behavior: Attached is a short mapping (dataflow-mapping.xlsx) that highlights where request metadata, KV cache, and long-term logs are stored. Short for now but Karthik will run a deeper export. Note: our KV cache is ephemeral by default (TTL-based) and is stored in the runtime region; cross-region replication only happens for selected failover groups (we do not replicate customer KV to other regions without an explicit config).

Proposed immediate actions:
- I will send the DPA redline and the mapping now (attached).
- Mina will draft suggested language for a conditional residency exception and a GLBA addendum by EOD tomorrow.
- Schedule a 30-minute legal + ops call: Wed 5/5 10:00-10:30 PT or Thu 5/6 13:00-13:30 PT — which works for your team?

If acceptable, I can also prepare a short mutual action plan (MAP) and push the DocuSign envelope to your procurement team.

Thanks — talk soon,
Sergio Alvarez
Principal Solutions Architect

Suggested DPA / GLBA approach (high level):
- Add a Schedule X (GLBA Addendum) that maps Redwood obligations to GLBA Safeguards Rules and the definitions GreenBank expects. This avoids changing the master DPA semantics.
- For per-entity residency exceptions: draft a short residency-exception exhibit that can be appended per-account, with explicit operational limits (region, KV cache TTL, no cross-region replication, no offshoring of logs). If they need stronger guarantees, recommend Dedicated/Private path.
- Subprocessor gating: include a clause that for any residency exception we will: (a) list allowed subprocessors in the exhibit, (b) commit to no further subcontracting without 30-day notice, and (c) provide a SOC2 snapshot and KMS attestation for those subprocessors.

Open questions to resolve with Karthik / Ops:
- What TTL values do we feel comfortable contractually committing for KV cache? I would propose 30s–2m for classification flows, longer only on Dedicated.
- Can we provide a time-bound exception for known failover groups (i.e., allow cross-region routing only during declared maintenance windows)?

I can draft the exhibit language; Sergio, if you can confirm the TTL/maintenance policy we will be ready to send a redline back to GreenBank.

—Mina

Sergio / Mina — thanks for the rapid turnaround and for the attachments. The compliance team reviewed the redline and has two asks: 

1) Can Redwood commit to a KV cache contractual TTL of <= 120s for the classification path (we took Mina's proposed 30s–2m window and want the upper bound in contract).
2) For the failover/maintenance windows where cross-region routing might occur, we need a written guarantee that (a) affected requests will be reprocessed in-region after failback and (b) we will be notified 48 hours in advance for planned maintenance that could trigger cross-region routing.

If those two items are contractually feasible, we can proceed to a DocuSign envelope for the DPA + Schedule X. Can you prepare the final exhibit and route via DocuSign to procurement (procurement@greenbank.com)? We can sign on our side once the exhibit and the TTL value are explicit.

Best,
